SK3051 The async method has no CancellationToken to forward

An async method that accepts no CancellationToken and calls something that would have taken one.

CategoryAsync
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

SK3004 reports a token accepted and not passed on. This reports the step before it: the method accepts none, so there is nothing to pass on and no caller can stop the work. The two are the same argument at two points in the call graph, and applying this rule's fix is what makes SK3004 reachable on the same body — a cancellation chain is worth nothing until it is complete, and the place it breaks first is the frame that never offered the parameter.

Example

Instead of:

async Task<string> LoadAsync(string path) {
    return await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path);
}

Write:

async Task<string> LoadAsync(string path, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) {
    return await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path, cancellationToken);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ The finding needs a call in the body that would have taken a token, and that exemption is what separates a finding from advice. "Every async method should accept a token" fires on every leaf in every codebase; "this method calls something that offers a token and has none to give it" names a concrete cancellation that is broken, and the callee appears in the message. The call must match one of the two shapes SK3004 can repair — an omitted optional CancellationToken parameter, or an overload that is this parameter list with a token appended and every argument positional — so the two rules cannot disagree about whether a call wants a token. ⚠ `SK3004` and this rule are disjoint on any one call, and the construction is the count: SK3004 reports a call with exactly one token in scope, and a call is evidence here only when there are none. ⚠ The claim is per call and not per body, and the difference was measured rather than assumed. The draft carried a second, method-level "declares no CancellationToken" check that would have made the stronger claim true; sabotaging it turned nothing red, because the scopes enclosing a call inside a body are a superset of the ones enclosing its declaration — so a method with a token parameter can never contain a call with none, and the check was dead code no sabotage could kill. It is gone. ⚠ Worse, the negative fixture that was supposed to pin the count was named cancellationToken and was being silenced by the CS0100 guard before the count was ever consulted; it is named token now, and sabotaging the count turns it red. ⚠ A call inside a `catch` or a `finally` is not evidence, because SK3004 declines to forward a token into cleanup and reporting the method would leave a finding whose only repair the sibling rule then refuses. ⚠ The rule is `Compilation`-scoped and the fix is what costs it. Appending a parameter — even an optional one — breaks a method group conversion, because optional parameters do not participate in delegate conversion and Func<Task> f = LoadAsync; becomes CS0123. Whether a method is used that way is not visible in the file that declares it, so the analysis collects every name used as a method group across the compilation and reports only methods no such use names; the name check is over-broad on purpose, so any occurrence of the identifier in a non-invoked position silences the rule. The price is that the rule is not cacheable, which is the same trade SK3001 states. ⚠ Not reported: override, virtual, abstract, new, partial and extern methods, interface implementations, anything carrying an attribute, Main, test code — by the enclosing method's attribute or by the enclosing type holding a test case ([#319]) — a parameter list ending in params (CS0231 leaves no edit), a method that already has a parameter named cancellationToken, and any method whose return type is not Task, Task<T>, ValueTask or ValueTask<T> — which is what keeps async void out of it. Generated code is excluded. The fix is unsafe because a parameter added to a signature is a signature the author should look at.
